name: Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32-S3 Sense
notes: Primary witness board: camera, PDM mic, microSD, 8 MB octal PSRAM. External u.FL antenna required — WiFi and BLE (pairing + offline console) need it seated; without it Bluetooth may not work at all.
thermal_notes: Camera PEEK + Wi-Fi bursts are the heat sources; sustained capture warms the sensor (image noise). Runtime gauge is the die-temp watchdog (FEATURE_DIAGNOSTICS). In enclosures, give the camera ribbon and u.FL antenna airspace and derate PEEK cadence before the watchdog throttles.

name: Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32-S3 (plain, non-Sense)
notes: Grove Vision AI V2 Kit pairing; external u.FL antenna required.
thermal_notes: Light duty — inference runs on the Vision AI module, not this host. Die-temp watchdog covers it; no special measures.

name: Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32-C3
notes: Stacks directly on the Grove Vision AI V2 XIAO socket; external u.FL antenna required.
thermal_notes: C3 at Vision-host duty runs cool; no special measures.

name: AI-Thinker ESP32-CAM
notes: The most-owned camera dev board in existence (~$6, OV2640). Release-level canary build with camera PEEK + Wi-Fi CSI + SPI-mode SD + pull-OTA; no mic, no free pins for GNSS/touch/IR, no classic-ESP32 tsens. Flashing is external-UART only (GPIO0 low at reset) — desktop Flasher / esptool, not the browser flasher. Promote with a hardware test report.
thermal_notes: Camera + Wi-Fi bursts on a thumb-sized PCB with no thermal relief; the notorious brown-out reboots are usually the 5 V supply, not heat. No die-temp watchdog on classic ESP32 — derate PEEK cadence in enclosures by design margin, not by telemetry.

name: ESP32-WROOM-32 DevKit (generic)
notes: The most common 'an ESP32' that people own (DevKitC / DOIT V1 / NodeMCU-32S / clones). Wi-Fi CSI presence witness with the signed chain and pull-OTA; no camera/mic/SD/PSRAM. GNSS optional on the free UART2. Promote with a hardware test report.
thermal_notes: Open-air devkit at CSI-witness duty runs cool; no special measures. No die-temp watchdog on classic ESP32.

name: Freenove ESP32-S3-WROOM CAM (FNK0085)
notes: The default Amazon 'ESP32-S3 camera kit' a US newcomer receives. Same S3 base as the flagship, camera on the Espressif S3-EYE reference map (entirely different pins — hence its own OTA product). microSD slot is 1-bit SDMMC only (no DAT3/CS routed), so the SPI-mode storage driver can't use it: SD off until an SDMMC path exists. No mic. Promote with a hardware test report.
thermal_notes: Same S3 heat sources as the flagship (camera PEEK + Wi-Fi bursts) on a larger PCB with more copper — runs cooler than the XIAO. Die-temp watchdog covers it.

name: ESP32-C3 Super Mini
notes: The most-owned sub-$3 board in the hobby (white-label, dozens of storefront names). Vision AI host over a Grove cable on the same GPIO4/5 map as the generic DevKit entry; own OTA product because the onboard LED differs (plain active-low GPIO8 vs the DevKit's WS2812). Clone antenna quality varies. Promote with a hardware test report.
thermal_notes: C3 at Vision-host duty runs cool; no special measures.

name: ESP32-C3 DevKitM-1 (generic)
notes: Generic C3 devkit wired to the Vision AI over a Grove cable (device guide §5). Promote with a hardware test report.
thermal_notes: Open-air devkit at Grove-cable duty; negligible.

name: Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32-C6 (MR60BHA2 mmWave kit)
notes: 60 GHz FMCW radar witness host. Radar decoder + FSMs are host-tested; end-to-end bench validation pending.
thermal_notes: The MR60 radar dissipates on its own PCB; keep the radome off hot surfaces and out of appliance exhaust — the radar noise floor rises with temperature.

name: Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32-S3 + Round Display
notes: Watch-puck fleet display: GC9A01 240x240 round LCD, CST816S touch, PCF8563 RTC, battery. External u.FL antenna required for reliable WiFi/BLE (the BLE 5 long-range fleet scan needs it seated). Bench validation pending — run docs/hardware/display_bench_bringup.md Track W to promote.
thermal_notes: Backlight + battery charging share one small puck; charging warms the PCF8563 crystal (clock drift). Dim the panel while charging.

name: Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-4.3
notes: Dash fleet display: 800x480 RGB565 parallel panel, GT911 5-point touch, CH422G IO expander. Bench validation pending — run docs/hardware/display_bench_bringup.md Track D to promote.
thermal_notes: The 800x480 backlight dominates the budget; full brightness in a case raises die temp — night dimming doubles as the thermal relief valve.

name: Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-4.3B
notes: Industrial-IO dash SKU + dev playground host: same 800x480 panel/GT911/CH422G as the 4.3, plus isolated DI0/DI1 + DO0/DO1, RS485, dedicated CAN, I2C sensor header, 6-36 V supply. Playground bring-up doc: docs/hardware/dev_playground_43b.md.
thermal_notes: Same panel thermals as the 4.3, plus the isolated DI/DO, RS485, and CAN transceivers add standing dissipation from the 6-36 V supply — ventilate the enclosure.

name: Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-4.3C
notes: The mic-bearing 'AI voice' dash sibling (sold as 4.3C-BOX, cased, mic grille on top): same 800x480 panel family (ST7701 controller - VERIFY init) + GT911 + CH422G, plus an ES8311/ES7210 audio stack fronting a dual-MIC array, a PCF85063 RTC (register map differs from the family PCF8563 - driver follow-up), and a BOX-edition terminal strip with functions to VERIFY. A DISTINCT privacy surface: own env (canary-display-dash-mic), own OTA product, mic off by default, alarm-pattern scalars only, hard mute = driver uninstalled, on-glass indicator while listening. Contract: docs/hardware/display_mic_variant.md.
thermal_notes: Cased BOX edition traps heat from the backlight + ES8311/ES7210 audio stack. Hold brightness headroom so the on-glass mic indicator stays readable, and ventilate the case.

name: Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32-C6 (Sentinel Standard head)
notes: Canary Sentinel Standard/Heavy sensor head: MR60BHA2 60 GHz radar + PIR + BH1750 lux, WiFi-RF/CSI + BLE on the onboard radio. Phase 0 — the board-agnostic fusion core is host-tested (firmware/common/fusion, firmware/tests_host); the on-device PlatformIO build + bench validation are pending (see firmware/projects/canary-sentinel), so not yet in flavors.json and used_by is empty until it phases in like canary-sense.
thermal_notes: PIR needs thermal stability — mount the sensor head clear of the C6's own warmth and of drafts; the radar noise floor rises with temperature.

name: Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32-C3 (Sentinel Lite)
notes: Canary Sentinel Lite: PIR + BH1750 lux, WiFi-RF + BLE on the onboard radio, NO radar/CSI (honest low-cost tier limit). Phase 0 — fusion core host-tested; on-device build + bench pending (firmware/projects/canary-sentinel), so not yet in flavors.json and used_by is empty.
thermal_notes: PIR needs thermal stability — keep the sensor stalk clear of the MCU and out of drafts.

name: Waveshare ESP32-C3-LCD-1.47
notes: Nightstand Line pocket node ('Canary Nightlight'): ST7789T portrait SPI driven 180x320/offset-30 per the vendor demo (marketing says 172x320 — see the board README), LCD CS/RST + SD CS + BACKLIGHT PWM all behind Waveshare's I2C EXIO expander at 0x24 (no LEDC backlight pin), QMI8658 IMU on the shared bus, NO WS2812 — the glass itself is the lamp. Single-core C3, NO PSRAM (lean single-buffer). Wired as the canary-display 'nightlight' flavor on the core-2.x display base (env canary-display-nightlight-c3): display_1in47.cpp EXIO path + nightlight_ui.cpp. Pin map from the vendor engineering-sample repo + schematic (they agree); bench validation pending.
thermal_notes: Enclosed pocket case (canary_c3_lcd147.scad) with a lamp duty cycle: the nightlight flavor hard-caps backlight duty at 50% in the HAL — a heat budget, not a preference. Thermally trivial below that cap.

name: Waveshare ESP32-C6-LCD-1.47
notes: Nightstand Line display: ST7789 172x320 SPI (34-px column offset) + 1x WS2812 ambient LED (GPIO8, RMT), single-core C6, NO PSRAM (lean single-buffer). Wired as the canary-display 'nightstand' flavor on the core-3.x display base (env canary-display-nightstand-c6: pioarduino platform + GFX 1.6.6 / LVGL 9.x / NimBLE 2.x — the same core-3 library row the Arduino CI proves): display_1in47.cpp HAL + portrait_ui.cpp + ambient_led.cpp. Bench validation pending (docs/hardware/display_nightstand_line.md §7).
thermal_notes: Coolest display in the fleet: single-core C6 + a 1.47" backlight. Nightstand duty is thermally trivial, and night dimming already floors what little there is.

name: Waveshare ESP32-C6-LCD-1.69
notes: Nightstand Line candidate (battery/pocket glance node): ST7789V2 240x280 SPI (20-px ROW offset), QMI8658 IMU + PCF85063 RTC on a shared I2C bus, 3.7 V MX1.25 battery with onboard charging, and a vendor-marketed 'AI speech' path (ES8311 codec + mic — treat as MIC-BEARING, mic off by default, until the schematic proves otherwise; same posture as the 4.3C). PARTIAL pin map: the vendor wiki was unreachable from the CI sandbox, so pins.h commits only chip facts + the family-shared ST7789 block and marks the rest -1 VERIFY (boards/waveshare-esp32c6-lcd169/README.md). Not in any build env yet.
thermal_notes: Battery charging warms the PCB next to the PCF85063 crystal (clock drift) and the QMI8658 (bias) — charge with the backlight dimmed and don't calibrate the IMU mid-charge. Die-temp watchdog is the runtime gauge.

name: Waveshare ESP32-S3-LCD-1.47
notes: Nightstand Line display (USB-A stick): SAME ST7789 172x320 panel as the C6 sibling but every display pin differs; 1x WS2812 ambient LED (GPIO38, RMT), dual-core S3 with 8 MB PSRAM, native USB. Wired as the canary-display 'nightstand' flavor (env canary-display-nightstand-s3): display_1in47.cpp HAL + portrait_ui.cpp + ambient_led.cpp. Bench validation pending (docs/hardware/display_nightstand_line.md).
thermal_notes: USB-A stick body: S3 + octal PSRAM heat-soak into a small stick that plugs into an already-warm port. The double-buffered animation budget is the throttle knob; die-temp watchdog is the gauge.

name: Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-1.69
notes: Nightstand Line TOUCH member (battery glance node): ST7789V2 240x280 SPI (20-px ROW offset) + CST816T capacitive touch, QMI8658 IMU + PCF85063 RTC on shared I2C, 3.7 V MX1.25 battery with onboard charging, PWR button, S3R8 (16 MB flash / 8 MB octal PSRAM). Wired as the canary-display 'touch169' flavor (env canary-display-touch169: nightstand app + FEATURE_TOUCH — display_1in47.cpp grows the double-gated CST816 path, portrait_ui.cpp reads geometry from pins.h). Pin map reconciled against the vendor GPIO/peripheral pinout table (2026-07): corrected RTC_INT (GPIO9->GPIO39), filled the power latch (SYS_EN=GPIO41/SYS_OUT=GPIO40), added the buzzer (GPIO42), QMI8658 INT (GPIO38) and the I2C device addresses (0x15/0x6B/0x51); only backlight polarity and the INT edges still want a bench check. Bench validation pending.
thermal_notes: Battery charging + the S3R8 render load stack on one small PCB: charging warms the PCF85063 crystal (drift) and QMI8658 (bias) — charge with the backlight dimmed, don't calibrate the IMU mid-charge. CST816 touch drifts when hot; keep the glass out of direct sun. The night backlight floor doubles as the thermal relief valve.

name: Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-7
notes: Nightstand Line big glass: 7" 800x480 RGB565 parallel + GT911 5-point touch + CH422G IO expander (backlight + touch-reset) — electrically the 4.3" Canary Dash at 7", so it reuses the dash RGB HAL/GT911/CH422G. Requires the 8 MB octal PSRAM for the 768 KB framebuffer. Wired as TWO canary-display products on the same glass: the wall 'dash7' flavor (env canary-display-dash7 — dash config + pins only, same HAL/UI) and the bedside 'nightstand7' flavor (env canary-display-nightstand7 — same RGB HAL/GT911/CH422G, its own clock-hero face, red night clock focus, and the lantern night light). Full 5-point touch gestures + bench validation pending (docs/hardware/display_nightstand_line.md).
thermal_notes: The hottest board in the fleet: a 7" backlight plus continuous 800x480 RGB refresh out of octal PSRAM. Backlight duty (via the CH422G) is the main relief valve and the die-temp watchdog (FEATURE_DIAGNOSTICS) the gauge; keep the GT911 glass out of direct sun — capacitive touch drifts when hot.

name: Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-AMOLED-2.06
notes: The wrist board, shared by two Phase-0 projects (host-tested cores in CI, no PlatformIO env until the hardware lands): canary-tincan (two siblings tie a string) and canary-companion (the Night Watch bedside clock + the Pocket Canary virtual pet): 2.06" 410x502 AMOLED (CO5300, 4-lane QSPI, brightness is a panel command — no backlight pin), FT3168 touch @0x38, QMI8658 IMU, PCF85063 RTC, AXP2101 PMU + Li-po (battery not included). Pin map transcribed from the vendor sample tree, not bench validated. Two traps: Waveshare's store copy says CST9220 touch but every vendor sketch drives an FT3168 — confirm first at bring-up; and there is NO vibration motor, so a DRV2605L + LRA on the exposed I²C port (0x5A) is required hardware for a watch whose whole premise is a knock you feel. Mics are present and deliberately unused — HAS_MICROPHONE 0 describes what the firmware may touch, not what is soldered.
thermal_notes: Skin contact, so thermals are a comfort question before they are a silicon one. AMOLED on a mostly-black face is cheap and the panel is off most of the time (wake-on-raise); the real budget is radio duty. Charging a Li-po against a wrist is the case to watch — dock it, don't wear it charging.

name: Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-AMOLED-2.41
notes: The flagship glance glass (V2 board, metal case): 2.41" 450x600 AMOLED (RM690B0, 4-lane QSPI, 16-px column window, brightness is a panel command — no backlight pin), FT6336 touch @0x38 with its INT behind the TCA9554 expander @0x20 (poll — there is no GPIO to attach), QMI8658 IMU, PCF85063 RTC, dedicated SDMMC 1-bit microSD, ETA6098 Li-po charger (autonomous — no I2C PMU; battery telemetry is the GPIO17 divider), soft power latch + panel supply on GPIO16 (drive HIGH early on battery), readable PWR case button on GPIO15. Wired as the canary-display 'amoled241' flavor (env canary-display-amoled241: nightstand app + CD_AMOLED_GLASS — display_amoled241.cpp QSPI HAL, portrait_ui.cpp scales its row metrics up on the tall glass). Pin map transcribed from the bench-tested CircuitPython board definition + the V2 case label; not OUR bench validation.
thermal_notes: AMOLED with a mostly-black face is the coolest glass in the display line — no backlight, and true black emits nothing. The metal case is its own heatsink; the real watch item is Li-po charging inside it (charge with the panel dim, and calibrate the battery divider before trusting a percentage).
